KIDS GAMES LESSON · KIDS GAMES · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Balloon Keep-Up — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches balloon keep-up in five steps — the game where one rule does all the work.

What is this?

Balloon keep-up is a tapping game: one balloon, everyone playing, and the balloon may never touch the floor.

What does it mean?

Keeping something afloat takes watching, waiting and gentle taps at the right moment — timing, learned with the softest object in the house.

What does the child need to know?

You need one blown-up balloon and a little clear space. Everyone who can reach the balloon can play — no teams, no turns, just keep it up.

Why this matters

A balloon falls slowly, so young players can watch it coming and choose their tap. It is the gentlest catching-and-hitting game ever invented.

What it teaches

Hand-eye timing, gentle-touch control (hard taps send balloons sideways), and quick feet that get the body where the balloon is going.

Words to learn

balloontapupfloatfloorgentlyagain

Say this to your child

“"The balloon is sleepy — tap it up! Gently, gently... it floats! Catch it with a tap before it touches the floor!"”

Step by step

  1. Blow up the balloon and let it float down between you.
  2. Say the rule: "the balloon may never touch the floor."
  3. Tap it up with an open hand — not a slap, a lift.
  4. Chase it wherever it drifts and tap it up again.
  5. Count the saves together — every tap is one point for the whole family.

Look closer at the picture

On the card, two open hands reach up toward one pink balloon — the hands are open because a flat, gentle tap is the whole secret of the game.

Ask your child

"How many taps did we do?" "What happens if we tap too hard?" "Can you save it with your head?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might shout "mine, mine!" and run the balloon down the hallway, count every tap out loud, or invent a rule where the balloon touching a grown-up is double points.

Out in the real world

Every party, every birthday, every picnic with a balloon becomes this game in about nine seconds — now your child knows how to run it.

Try it together

Harder ways: one hand behind your back, everyone sitting cross-legged (the balloon may only fly as high as your head), or two balloons at once for the championship round.

Understanding check

Ask: "What is the one rule?" (the balloon never touches the floor) "Do we slap it or tap it?" (tap it gently)

This lesson pairs with the Balloon Keep-Up flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Kids Games.
